title: Update on Tripartite Discussions on Advance Mandatory Retrenchment Notification
what_it_is: Update on Tripartite Discussions on Advance Mandatory Retrenchment Notification

sections.label: Mandatory retrenchment notification requirement
sections.summary: Firms with 10 or more employees must submit a mandatory retrenchment notification to MOM within five working days of notifying retrenched employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: At present, firms with 10 or more employees are required to submit a mandatory retrenchment notification (MRN) to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) within five working days of notifying employees of their retrenchment.

sections.label: Earlier retrenchment notification review
sections.summary: In 2025, 77% of MRNs came at least seven days ahead and 73% at least two weeks ahead, while tripartite partners study encouraging earlier notification.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In 2025, 77% of MRNs were submitted at least seven days ahead of the employee's last working day and 73% of MRNs were submitted at least two weeks ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As part of an ongoing review of the Employment Act, tripartite partners are studying how to encourage earlier notification by employers – both to affected employees and to the Government.

sections.label: Penalties for non-compliance
sections.summary: Non-compliance carries an administrative penalty of $1,000 for the first contravention and $2,000 for subsequent contraventions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Currently, the penalty for non-compliance is an administrative penalty of $1,000 for the first contravention and $2,000 for subsequent contraventions.

sections.label: Retrenched worker placement outcomes
sections.summary: For 2022 to 2024, seven in 10 retrenched workers coached by Workforce Singapore or e2i were placed within six months, median about three months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What we have is that for the last three years ending 2024 – that means 2022, 2023 and 2024 – seven in 10 retrenched workers, who have received career coaching from both Workforce Singapore and/or the Employment and Employability Institute's (e2i's) career coaches, were actually placed within six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The median time to placement averaged around three months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, the Taskforce for Responsible Retrenchment and Employment Facilitation reaches out to all retrenched locals with available contact details to provide them with employment facilitation support.

sections.label: Possible effect on retrenchment negotiations
sections.summary: This may push companies to finalise retrenchments faster and therefore discourage such backend negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Because this may – and I want to emphasise that this may – push companies to finalise the retrenchments faster and therefore, discourage such backend negotiations.
